page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance configured on KVM hypervisor architecture. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8475B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, this instance delivers 12 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 24.0 GB of system memory. The physical topology yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core.

Networking performance is rated at a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage for system files and persistent data. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance upon deployment. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the tight RAM-to-vCPU allocation reduces resource overhead for workloads that demand processing power over memory capacity.

The ecs.c8i.3xlarge is architected for compute-bound workloads, including continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) build nodes, application web servers, batch job processing, and distributed microservice workloads. The primary operational tradeoff is the limited memory capacity relative to core count, rendering it less suited for large in-memory databases or memory-intensive data analytics.

The instance features a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no bundled local storage, depending entirely on remote block storage solutions for data persistence. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.3xlarge is well-matched for compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, application servers, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and web serving.
